title: Important Notice for Residents: USPS Policy Change Could Affect Timeliness of Property Tax Payments - NewsBreak
text:
1 hours ago The Oneida County Treasurer is informing residents about a change in U.S. Postal Service policy that may affect property tax payments. Starting in August 2025, the USPS will apply postmarks at regional sorting centers instead of when mail is first handled. This may delay the official postmark date by several days after mailing.
This change matters because many federal and state laws use the USPS postmark as proof of timely payment. If tax payments are mailed close to the deadline, they may receive a late postmark and be considered late, even if mailed before the due date. This could lead to late fees for taxpayers.
The Treasurer advises mailing tax payments early to avoid these issues. Residents are also advised not to use personal bank online bill pay services, as these payments may not get a postmark and could arrive late. Taxpayers can also bring payments to the post office and request a postmark or use certified mail for confirmation.
